plan_name: Seven-day low-waste family meal and shopping plan
assumptions: Shopping takes place Thursday 10 September 2026 and the seven-day plan runs Friday 11 September through Thursday 17 September 2026.
The plan is sized for four people, the upper end of the stated 3–4-person range, except Thursday leftover lunch which explicitly provides two leftover portions plus pantry alternatives.
Pantry quantities are copied from the workbook. Where the workbook gives no unit, a practical unit such as pack, tin, carton, jar or bag is inferred from the item name.

The Pantry tab contains no use-by dates. To satisfy the schema, planning review dates are assigned: 13 September for highly perishable fresh items, 17 September for chilled/open items, 31 December 2026 for frozen items and 10 September 2027 for shelf-stable items. Check every printed date and override these assumptions.

Workbook prices are used where listed for essentials, snacks and household products. Prices for meal-specific fresh ingredients are planning estimates in pounds and should be checked at the chosen shop.
No allergies or dietary restrictions were supplied beyond soy milk and dairy-free weekly baking. Verify all labels, especially gluten-free needs suggested by the pantry food box.
Items shown as 0 to buy are included in the shopping list to make pantry deductions explicit and must be quantity-checked before shopping.

breakfast.meal: Toast with jam or peanut butter, strawberries and grapes
breakfast.notes: Uses the most delicate pantry fruit first. Use the existing wraps toasted if no bread is open.

lunch.meal: Ham and cream-cheese wraps with hummus and clementines
lunch.notes: Uses the existing sliced meat, wraps, cream cheese and hummus early. Keep one clementine back if needed for a later snack.

dinner.meal: Scottish mussels with chips, peas and bread
dinner.notes: Use the pantry mussels on the first day because they are the most time-sensitive item. Serve the existing frozen chips and peas; discard any mussels that do not open after cooking.

breakfast.notes: Uses four pantry eggs and existing frozen berries. Make a double stack only if there is freezer space; cooked pancakes freeze well.

lunch.notes: Uses two pantry tins of mackerel, pantry rice and frozen vegetables, avoiding another fresh protein purchase.

dinner.meal: Chicken fajita wraps with fresh salsa
dinner.notes: Cook while lettuce and peppers are fresh. Use the pantry frozen chicken pieces, wraps and seasonings. Make salsa during the afternoon preparation session.

breakfast.meal: Ready Break with soy milk and banana
breakfast.notes: A quick breakfast before the roast. Slice only the bananas needed so the rest remain available for banana bread and snacks.

lunch.meal: Beans on toast with grated cheese
lunch.notes: Uses one pantry tin of beans and existing cheese. Freeze half the new loaf on shopping day so it stays fresh for later lunches.

dinner.meal: Roast chicken dinner with roast potatoes, carrots, broccoli and peas
dinner.notes: Roast a chicken large enough to leave about 500 g cooked meat. Cool leftovers promptly: reserve for Monday and Tuesday lunches, and freeze Tuesday’s portion if not using within 48 hours.

breakfast.meal: Cereal with soy milk and blueberries
breakfast.notes: Opens the purchased blueberries early in the week. Use pantry oat milk first if the soy milk is not yet needed elsewhere.

lunch.notes: Uses reserved roast chicken and existing mayonnaise. Add leftover lettuce from fajitas to prevent waste.

dinner.meal: Spaghetti Bolognese with carrot, celery and onion
dinner.notes: Carrot and celery keep well after the weekend. Make six portions: serve four and chill or freeze two for Thursday lunch.

breakfast.meal: Toast with peanut butter and banana
breakfast.notes: Uses ripe bananas and pantry peanut butter. Take bread from the freezer the night before.

lunch.notes: Uses the final safely stored roast chicken. If there is less than four portions, supplement with one pantry tin of tuna.

dinner.notes: Freeze the salmon on shopping day and thaw overnight Monday; this lets the plan use fragile salad produce first without risking the fish.

breakfast.meal: Ready Break with soy milk and mixed berries
breakfast.notes: Frozen berries give variety without adding late-week fresh-fruit waste.

lunch.meal: Leek, potato and carrot soup with bread
lunch.notes: Uses the remaining celery, carrots and potatoes. Make six portions and freeze two for an easy future lunch.

dinner.meal: Jacket potatoes with tuna, cheese and beans
dinner.notes: Uses pantry tuna, beans and cheese. Bake four medium-large potatoes; any extra filling can top Thursday toast.

breakfast.meal: Cereal with soy milk and banana
breakfast.notes: Finishes opened cereal, soy milk and remaining ripe banana near the end of the plan.

lunch.notes: Use the two extra portions made Monday. The other two people can use pantry ready meals or soup portions if four lunches are required.

dinner.meal: Fish fingers, chips, peas and beans
dinner.notes: A freezer-led final dinner prevents late-week spoilage and uses pantry breaded fish, chips, peas and the remaining tin of beans.

weekly_preparations.name: Dairy-free banana bread
weekly_preparations.storage: Keep 3 days airtight; freeze remaining slices for up to 3 months.
weekly_preparations.notes: Use 3 very ripe bananas, 250 g self-raising flour, 100 g sugar, 2 eggs, 75 ml oil and a little soy milk. Pantry eggs, sugar and oil reduce the purchase requirement.

weekly_preparations.name: Fresh tomato salsa
weekly_preparations.storage: Refrigerate covered and use within 2 days.
weekly_preparations.notes: Prepare shortly before dinner from tomatoes, onion, lime and optional hot sauce. Make only one bowl because fresh salsa does not keep well.

weekly_preparations.name: Dairy-free oat and raisin cookies
weekly_preparations.storage: Airtight for 5 days; freeze baked cookies for up to 2 months.
weekly_preparations.notes: Use pantry sugar, oil and raisins purchased as snacks; oats and flour are shared with breakfasts and banana bread. Freeze half immediately to control waste.

waste_reduction_summary: Use pantry mussels, strawberries, grapes, sliced meat, wraps, hummus and chilled dairy first.
Freeze salmon and beef mince on shopping day; freeze the chicken only if its use-by date does not cover Sunday.
Freeze one sliced loaf immediately and remove only the slices needed.
Cook a larger Sunday chicken and a six-portion Monday Bolognese so planned leftovers replace extra lunch purchases.
Share carrots, celery, onions, potatoes and broccoli across multiple dinners and Wednesday soup.
Freeze half the banana bread and cookies, plus surplus soup, to prevent snack and batch-cook waste.
Check quantities in opened pantry bags before shopping; buy only the noted fallback item if stock is insufficient.
